bib.title: CogVLM: Visual Expert for Pretrained Language Models

question: Can a pretrained LLM gain strong visual understanding without losing its NLP ability, by deep fusion rather than shallow alignment?
hypothesis: A trainable visual expert (separate QKV and FFN for image tokens in every layer) beats shallow alignment and avoids the forgetting caused by training the LLM itself on image-text data.
contributions: CogVLM deeply integrates visual and linguistic features while retaining the full capabilities of a pretrained LLM; CogVLM-17B, trained from Vicuna-7B, achieves state-of-the-art across 17 classic cross-modal benchmarks
Ablations validate the visual expert and deep fusion, and examine visual encoder scale, attention masks, the most impactful parameters and image SSL loss
Weights and the SFT-phase dataset released

method.summary: CogVLM adds to a frozen Vicuna-1.5-7B a frozen EVA2-CLIP-E ViT, a two-layer SwiGLU MLP adapter and, in every layer, a trainable visual expert (own QKV matrix and FFN for image tokens, initialised from the LLM). Two-stage pretraining on about 1.5B image-text pairs plus 40M grounding images, then SFT into CogVLM-Chat and CogVLM-Grounding.
method.task: vision-language pretraining and instruction tuning (captioning, VQA, grounding)

datasets.name: LAION-2B + COYO-700M (filtered)
datasets.preprocessing: removed broken URLs, NSFW images, noisy captions, images with political bias, aspect ratio > 6 or < 1/6

datasets.name: Visual grounding set (from LAION-115M)
datasets.source: LAION-115M, subset of LAION-400M filtered by Li et al. 2023b
datasets.preprocessing: nouns by spaCy, boxes by GLIPv2; retained subset so over 75% of images have at least two boxes

datasets.name: SFT data for CogVLM-Chat
datasets.source: VQAv2, OKVQA, TextVQA, OCRVQA, ScienceQA, LLaVA-Instruct, LRV-Instruction, LLaVAR
datasets.preprocessing: LLaVA-Instruct errors manually corrected; prompts 'Question: Short answer:' for short VQA, 'Question: Answer:' for dialogue

datasets.name: Grounding SFT data for CogVLM-Grounding
datasets.source: Flickr30K Entities, RefCOCO/+/g, Visual7W, VisualGenome (about 86k images, 3.6M region-caption pairs), Grounded CoT-VQA
datasets.preprocessing: four task types GC, REG, REC, GroundedVQA; datasets converted between tasks

datasets.name: Eval benchmarks
datasets.split: NoCaps val, Flickr/COCO Karpathy test, TextCaps test, VQAv2 test-dev, OKVQA val, TextVQA val, MMBench test, MathVista test-mini etc.

models.name: CogVLM-17B
models.params: 17B total (6.5B trainable in pretraining; 6.6B in Table 4)
models.architecture: ViT + MLP adapter + GPT-style LLM + per-layer visual expert
models.init_from: Vicuna-1.5-7B; visual expert initialised from LLM weights

other.position_ids: all image tokens share one RoPE position id
other.mask: causal mask on all attention including image tokens

training.objective: Stage 1: next-token prediction on caption text; Stage 2: captioning plus REC as VQA with boxes [[x0,y0,x1,y1]] in 000-999, loss on Answer only; SFT: next-token on answers
training.compute: 230.1 PFLOPS*days pretraining; 1.2 VQAv2 finetune; 0.13 TextVQA finetune (Table 8)

other.resolution: 224x224 stage 1; 224 then 490x490 for last 30,000 stage-2 iterations; SFT at 490x490
other.sft_vit: ViT unfrozen in SFT at lr one-tenth

inference.prompting: 'Question: Short answer:' (short) or 'Question: Answer:' (extended); grounding questions 'Where is the object?'

metrics.name: GPT4 score
metrics.definition: MM-Vet and LLaVA-Bench judged by GPT-4

eval.protocol: Single reported numbers; no seeds, variance or significance tests stated. NoCaps and Flickr zero-shot; COCO and TextCaps finetuned. Many VQA numbers marked * were trained during SFT.

availability.data: SFT dataset stated to be released

evidence.quote: During the final 30,000 iterations, we change the input resolution from 224 × 224 to 490 × 490.

results.claim: Directly training the language part of a VLM on LAION drops MMLU to 24.9 at 2500 steps (catastrophic forgetting).
results.setup: LLM trained directly on LAION during multimodal pretraining (Fig 3)

results.claim: Cited: adapting an 8B LM for VLM pretraining can cut NLG performance by 87.3%.
results.quote: can lead to an 87.3% reduction in natural language generation

results.claim: Ablation: tuning only the MLP adapter (shallow alignment) is clearly worse than the visual expert on VQAv2.
results.setup: Table 4, 6,000 iterations, batch 8,192, 140M trainable params vs CogVLM 6.6B
results.table: Table 4, row MLP Adapter, column VQAv2 (73.8 vs 80.0 for CogVLM)

results.claim: Tuning all LLM parameters plus adapter (no visual expert, 6.9B) gets VQAv2 78.9 vs 80.0 for the visual expert at similar trainable size.
results.table: Table 4, row LLM+MLP Adapter, column VQAv2

results.claim: Visual expert at every 4th layer (1.7B trainable) is only slightly worse than every layer.
results.table: Table 4, row VE-full every 4th layer, column VQAv2

results.claim: Random initialisation of the expert is worse than initialising from the LLM on captioning and OKVQA.
results.table: Table 4, row Random init, column OKVQA

results.claim: Swapping EVA2-E (4.4B) for EVA2-L (300M) drops TextVQA by 2.5 points, little elsewhere.
results.quote: where we recorded a decline of 2.5

results.claim: Full (bidirectional) mask on visual tokens is slightly worse than causal on NoCaps and OKVQA; image SSL loss gives no gain.
results.table: Table 4, row Full mask, column NoCaps

results.claim: CogVLM base reaches NoCaps val OOD CIDEr 132.6 zero-shot, beating GIT2 (130.6) with 1.5B vs 12.9B pretraining pairs.
results.table: Table 1, row CogVLM, column NoCaps val OOD

results.claim: CogVLM zero-shot Flickr CIDEr 94.9, 9.1 above Qwen-VL.
results.quote: achieves a SOTA score of 94.9 surpassing the concurrently released Qwen-VL model by 9.1 points

results.claim: CogVLM-Chat VQAv2 82.3, TextVQA 70.4, ScienceQA 91.2 (* trained in SFT, except ScienceQA unstarred in text but starred in table).
results.note: Table 2 stars VQA sets as trained in SFT, so these are not zero-shot

results.claim: CogVLM-Chat on LVLM benchmarks: MM-Vet 51.1, SEED 72.5, MMBench 77.6, POPE 87.9, MMMU 41.1.
results.note: MathVista printed 34.5 in Table 2 but 35.2 in text

results.quote: 35.2 on the multimodal mathematical reasoning benchmark MathVista

results.claim: CogVLM-Grounding RefCOCO val 92.76, surpassing specialist UNINEXT-H 92.64.
results.quote: our model attains a score of 92.76, surpassing UNINEXT-H’s 92.64

results.claim: CogVLM achieves SOTA on 5 of 9 grounding splits vs specialists.
results.quote: achieving SOTA performance on 5 of 9 splits

results.claim: TDIUC overall accuracy 94.0 vs 88.2 previous SOTA (MUREL).
results.quote: resulting in a 94.0 accuracy score compared to the previous SOTA of 88.2

results.table: Table 8, row CogVLM, column Pretraining compute

results.claim: Visual expert doubles parameters, keeps FLOPs the same, and reproduces original LLM behaviour on text-only input.

limits: Authors name better SFT alignment, RLHF and anti-hallucination as unexplored; no text-only benchmark numbers after training are given to back the no-NLP-loss claim (only Fig 3 for the direct-training baseline).
Many Table 2 VQA numbers are on datasets trained in SFT (starred), so not zero-shot.
No seeds, variance, hardware or wall-clock reported; ablations are 6,000 iterations only.
Dataset sizes for the SFT mixtures are not given.
Ablation compares expert vs full-LLM tuning only at roughly matched trainable size, in one setting.

terms.definition: a trainable QKV matrix and MLP per layer, applied to image tokens, same shapes as and initialised from the pretrained LM
mapping image features into the input embedding space of a frozen LM via a Q-Former or linear layer

lineage.note: trainable LM params; data source LLaVA-Instruct (2304.08485)
motivating analogy: per-layer adaptation beats prefix (P-Tuning)

figures.caption: MMLU score and training loss over multimodal pre-training phase.
figures.why: Shows forgetting when the LLM is trained directly on LAION.

figures.caption: The architecture of CogVLM. Only the purple parts are trainable.
figures.why: Shows the per-layer split of QKV and FFN between image and text tokens.

figures.caption: Ablation studies for various components and training settings.
figures.why: Adapter-only vs LLM-tuning vs visual expert at matched settings.

code.snippet: Q = concat(X_I W^Q_I, X_T W^Q_T); FFN(X) = concat(FFN_I(X_I), FFN_T(X_T))

problems: Text extraction fine. Table 1 and 2 are flattened one cell per line; Fig 1 radar numbers are noise. No embedded instructions.
